t: LeetCode 3185 – Count Pairs That Form a Complete Day II
o: Count pairs i < j with (hours[i] + hours[j]) % 24 == 0. Only residues mod 24 matter: a pair completes a day iff their residues sum to 0 mod 24. In example 1 residues are [12,12,6,0,0]; the two (12,12) and one... actually (3,4) are the (0,0) pair, plus (0,1) — total 2 matching the expected output along with (3,4). With n up to 5·10^5, the O(n²) double loop (2.5·10^10 ops) is too slow, so we count residues in one pass.
k: Reduce every hour to its residue mod 24; pairs work iff residues are complementary (r and (24-r)%24).
One pass with a running residue-count array gives O(n).

a.n: Approach 1: Residue counting in one pass
a.i: Keep cnt[r] = how many earlier elements have residue r. For each new element with residue r, it pairs with all earlier elements of residue (24 - r) % 24, then increment cnt[r].
s: For each h: r = h % 24; ans += cnt[(24 - r) % 24]; cnt[r]++.
a.t: O(n) — a single pass with O(1) work per element

a.n: Approach 2: Brute force (for intuition / small inputs)
a.i: Check every pair directly. Simple and correct but quadratic — included to motivate the counting approach.
a.t: O(n²) — all pairs checked; too slow for n = 5·10^5

w: Always reach for the complement-residue trick on 'pair sums to multiple of m' problems. Pitfalls: use (24 - r) % 24 so residue 0 pairs with itself, and use a 64-bit accumulator since the answer can approach ~10^11. Follow-ups: pairs forming a multiple of an arbitrary d (same technique with d buckets), or counting triples.
